short: DTW pseudo targets (M02) follow prior EMG target transfer; the mode discriminator (M03) is untested by its ablation; silent MCD/STOI use self-made references and 18 speakers are dropped.
position: The paper [@zheng2023pseudo] changes the silent training target (M02) and adds joint silent-vocalized training with a speaking-mode discriminator (M03); both are standard. DTW transfer of vocalized targets to silent articulation, with realignment by the partially trained model, was established for silent EMG [@janke2017emg; @gaddy2020digital], uncited here. The mode discriminator has no earlier match among 12 domain-adversarial studies (pattern match, Appendix), but its single-run ablation also removes all vocalized training data. Silent MCD and STOI are scored against the method's own vocoded pseudo targets, and 18 of 81 speakers were dropped from the silent test by the same DTW cost (Sec. 4.2). The silent WER gain (59.960% to 43.114%, Table 1) is relatively smaller than the vocalized gain (28% against 36%, inference), so it shows better use of paired data, not a narrowed silent-vocalized gap.
